title: Receipts/ClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssemblyTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/2), passes on head (2/2); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1

refutes.claim: The reporter names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites: lines 735, 1009 and 1101. The change fixes only the two at 1009 and 1101 (new lines ~985 and ~1077); no hunk touches line 735. The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper cannot protect it, because the array index runs while the `Diagnostic` argument is built, before the wrapper is called. The reporter did not narrow down which site fires. If 735 is reached for a metadata member of `Item<T>`, the generator (CS8785) and the analyzer (AD0001) still crash. That would miss the criteria 'do not throw on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly' and 'diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the symbol has no declaring syntax'.

refutes.claim: The change only guards two diagnostic sites, and both sit inside `this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...)`. The generator does not report diagnostics (I believe it passes a null reporter; not checked). With a null reporter, `?.Invoke` never evaluates its arguments, so those two sites cannot have caused CS8785. The reporter named three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (735, 1009, 1101). The two fixed hunks match 1009 and 1101 (each offset by 27 lines). The third site, near old line ~708, has no hunk. It likely sits outside a `?.Invoke` and still throws when `GetObjectInfo` runs on a metadata `Item<int>`. If so, the generator still crashes and the app gets no resolver, so the requirement is not met.
